ACCEPTThe corrected written theorem package is mathematically sound. The earlier REVISE remains the correct verdict on the earlier text: its bridge-mate sentence was false. The replacement now agrees with the unchanged matching and correctly counts two new crossings and one internalized crossing.The new note establishes a stronger obstruction than the preceding example. Its complete  $8\times8$  configuration admits no nonempty endpoint-promotion bundle of any orientation, yet its central receiver has charge  $1$ . The all- $r$  construction, fixed charge, blank allocation, and one-tile exterior repair follow from the coordinates by general arguments.This acceptance concerns the supplied written mathematics and explicit constructions. I have not executed the code, verified a Lean build, or assessed novelty.1. The fixed-side threshold criterion is exactFor a fixed orientation of the matching from one bipartition side, let  $S$  be the set of edges chosen for promotion. For  $i\in S$ , the removed occupied neighbors of  $x_i$  are exactly:its own mate  $y_i$ ;the distinct mates  $y_j$  indexed by outgoing neighbors of  $i$  in  $D[S]$ .Matching disjointness and simplicity ensure that these are distinct vertices. Therefore
$$\deg_{A\setminus Y_S}(x_i)
=d_i-1-\operatorname{outdeg}_{D[S]}(i).$$
The bundle lemma consequently gives
$$S\text{ is feasible}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{outdeg}_{D[S]}(i)\ge \max(0,d_i-2)
\quad\text{for every }i\in S.$$
This formula includes occupied selected neighbors: they contribute to  $d_i$ , remain occupied, and cannot contribute to the outgoing-neighbor deletions. There is no omitted selected-neighbor condition.Peeling computes the greatest feasible subsetThe required invariant is:Every feasible subset remains contained in the current set of surviving vertices.If a vertex has too few outgoing neighbors in the current set, it cannot belong to a feasible subset of that set, since restricting the set cannot increase its outgoing count. Removing it therefore preserves the invariant.At termination the survivors satisfy all their thresholds, so they form a feasible subset themselves. They both contain every feasible subset and belong to the family being unioned. Hence they equal its union.This proves:existence of a greatest feasible subset, not merely an inclusion-maximal one;correctness of peeling;independence of the peeling order.Keeping the thresholds fixed during peeling is essential and correctly specified. Peeling removes candidate promotions from consideration; it does not physically remove their occupied endpoints. Recomputing occupied degrees during that process would change the problem.Given  $D$  and the thresholds, reverse adjacency lists allow each vertex and arc to be processed a bounded number of times, yielding the stated linear-time computation. Constructing those inputs requires the corresponding scan of the original configuration.Repeated actual core promotions terminate because every nonempty promotion deletes matching edges. Recomputing the graph and thresholds after each actual move is correct. Stopping when both sides have empty cores gives exactly the claimed absence of fixed-side bundles. It does not establish confluence of the resulting pair or completeness for mixed-side bundles.Degree-four scopeThe thresholds are indeed one for degree three and two for degree four. In the stated  $K_{4,4}$  example, the dependency digraph is the complete loopless directed graph on four vertices. Every vertex has outgoing count three and threshold two, so the full matching is a feasible core. Promoting one side leaves four independent selected vertices.Thus this is a valid strict distinction from the earlier single/degree-three-cycle moves on general bipartite graphs. The note correctly avoids claiming a strict grid separation from that abstract example.For precision, the earlier homogeneous-chain inequality already allows degree-four endpoints whenever its geometric hypotheses hold, because its degree assumption is  $\deg_A\ge3$ . What remains outside that inequality is general geometry not satisfying those chain hypotheses. The new core criterion supplies an exact promotion rule involving degree-four endpoints.2. The frozen-endpoint induction excludes mixed-side bundlesThe implication used in the proof has the correct direction:
$$\text{an endpoint cannot be promoted}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{its mate cannot be removed}.$$
It does not assert that a frozen endpoint itself must remain occupied.Fix any feasible promotion bundle, allowing arbitrary orientations. Original  $T$  vertices remain occupied. An original matching endpoint  $z$  can be removed only by promoting its mate on that original matching edge. Thus, once that mate has been excluded from every feasible bundle,  $z$  is guaranteed occupied in every such bundle.An endpoint with two distinct guaranteed occupied neighbors cannot be promoted, because it would then be selected with at least two occupied neighbors. Induction proves every freeze universally over feasible bundles.This argument remains valid when one bundle simultaneously uses both sides, both anchored paths, or several translated copies. There is no locality assumption restricting the bundle.The second round on an anchored path is not circularFor the path  $p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3$ :The two selected neighbors of each outer endpoint exclude  $p_0,p_3$ .Their mates  $p_1,p_2$  are therefore guaranteed occupied.The selected neighbor of  $p_1$ , together with the already guaranteed  $p_2$ , excludes  $p_1$ .The selected neighbor of  $p_2$ , together with the already guaranteed  $p_1$ , excludes  $p_2$ .The guarantees in steps 3–4 come from step 1, not from the new conclusions of steps 3–4.The certificate is sufficient; no converse has been established. Its scope is also correctly restricted to bundles using original matching edges and retaining original  $T$ . Changing the matching, deleting selected vertices, or adding previously blank vertices is outside this certificate.3. Unlike the preceding fixture, this establishes sharpness even after adding full endpoint-bundle terminality.5. The translated family is valid for every  $r\ge1$ The occupied support of copy  $i$  lies on rows
$$6i+1,\ldots,6i+6.$$
Successive copies have disjoint occupied supports. The only potentially adjacent occupied rows from consecutive copies are
$$6i+6,\qquad 6i+7.$$
Their occupied column sets are

which are disjoint. Hence no new occupied adjacency is introduced.The overlap of the nominal translated  $8\times8$  rectangles causes no conflict: the construction translates the sets  $T,M$ , and the occupied supports do not overlap. The last occupied row is  $6r$ , inside the ambient rows  $0,\ldots,6r+1$ .All selected degrees and all matching-endpoint degrees remain unchanged. The same frozen proof applies against any bundle on the entire graph, because every selected anchor remains occupied regardless of what the bundle does in another copy.Receiver geometryFor copy  $i$ , its central tiles lie in rows  $3i+1,3i+2$ , columns  $1,2$ . The bridge
$$E_i=(3i+3,1)$$
lies between the lower-left central tile of copy  $i$  and the upper-left central tile of copy  $i+1$ .All these tiles are distinct. Therefore the receiver is tile-connected and has

tiles.Each bridge has labels

B&B\\
B&T

so
$$t=1,\quad b=3,\quad p=0,\quad b-t=2,\quad \rho=-1.$$
It contains no matching endpoint and therefore introduces or internalizes no matching crossing.The crossings remain precisely
$$(6i+2,2)-(6i+2,1),\qquad
(6i+5,5)-(6i+5,6)$$
for each copy  $i$ . All are deficient-to-deficient. Thus
$$Q=k=2r,\qquad D=2r-2,\qquad
\sigma=\eta=0,\qquad j=2r,$$
and
$$2\rho(R_r)=-(2r-2)+2r=2.$$
This proves the asserted fixed positive charge for every  $r$ , without relying on a finite range of controls.6. The bridge’s private and unused blanks are correctly distinguishedUnder the agreed internal reservation convention, the bridge’s selected BR vertex is
$$(6i+7,3).$$
Its lexicographically first internal adjacent blank is TR:
$$(6i+6,3).$$
After reserving it, the free blanks are:Free blankOwner incidenceTL:  $(6i+6,2)$ Private to owner  $(3i+2,1)$ , through its selected BL corner  $(6i+5,2)$ BL:  $(6i+7,2)$ No adjacent selected corner of an internal saturated ownerThe classification of the second blank as unused deserves particular care. It is adjacent to selected vertices, including the bridge’s own  $T$  and a  $T$  in an exterior deficient tile. Those are not saturated-owner incidences. Its external lower neighbor is a  $P$  in the next central deficient tile. Therefore its degree in the owner-incidence construction is zero.The central deficient tiles leave no free blanks. Hence these bridge blanks constitute the entire free set:
$$c=2r,\qquad p=u=r-1,\qquad e=d=0.$$
The exact witness identity is
$$2\rho(R_r)
=2r-(r-1)-(r-1)
=2.$$
Every counted resource is a distinct physical blank. No reserved central blank or reserved bridge blank is counted again.The full-grid and exterior totals are also correct:
$$|T|=12r,\qquad |M|=4r,\qquad |T|+|M|=16r,$$

$$\rho(\text{whole grid})
=16r-\frac{8(6r+2)}2
=-8r-8,$$

The construction establishes arbitrarily large connected receiver size with charge  $1$ . It does not establish growing positive charge for those connected receivers.7. The one-tile exterior repair pays the debt exactly onceThe donor tile  $(0,1)$  has vertices
$$(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3)$$
and labels
$$\begin{matrix}
B&B\\
B&T
\end{matrix}.$$
Thus it has one selected vertex, three blanks, no matching endpoint, and no saturated attachment:
$$\rho_{(0,1)}=\frac{1-3}{2}=-1.$$
It is outside  $R_r$ , whose first tile row is  $1$ , and is adjacent to its tile  $(1,1)$ . Therefore adjoining it preserves tile connectivity and gives
$$\rho\bigl(R_r\cup\{(0,1)\}\bigr)=1-1=0.$$
The witness ledger confirms this independently. Reserving  $(0,3)$  leaves the two free blanks
$$(0,2),\qquad (1,2).$$
Neither has an adjacent saturated-owner selected corner, so both are unused blanks. For the augmented region,
$$D=2r,\quad k=Q=2r,\quad p=r-1,\quad u=r+1,$$
with  $c=2r$  and  $d=\sigma=\eta=0$ . Hence
$$2\rho=2r-(r-1)-(r+1)=0.$$
These two additional blanks were not present in the original receiver’s resource count. The donor is therefore counted once, with no reuse of the bridge compensation.The limitation to this exact donor is justified. For example, in the base fixture one can add  $(0,2)$  to  $T$ : its neighbors are blank, and no original selected or matching-endpoint degree is disturbed. The anchored obstruction remains, but tile  $(0,1)$  then has two diagonal selected vertices and charge zero. Thus the anchor assumptions alone do not force this particular donor to retain charge  $-1$ .8. The Lean statement has a sound conditional scopeBy inspection, the supplied proof is the stated structural induction:two_selected obtains two retained neighbors from hselected;selected_frozen obtains one from hselected and the other from the induction hypothesis through hretained;two_frozen obtains both through the two induction hypotheses and hretained.In each case, hfeasible forces the two neighbors to be equal, contradicting hdistinct.No finiteness, bipartiteness, symmetry, or matching-involution assumption is needed for this abstract conditional implication. Those properties belong to the physical interpretation.The physical adapter must use the right vertex domainThe hypothesisleanhretained : ∀ vertex, ¬ promoted (mate vertex) → retained vertexis universal over Vertex. It should not be instantiated naively on all grid vertices with retained meaning actual final occupancy. For the empty bundle, that would incorrectly require every original blank to be retained.A sound physical instantiation is:Vertex is the subtype of original occupied vertices  $A$ ;mate is the original matching involution on  $P$ , extended by the identity on  $T$ ;promoted is membership in the bundle’s promoted set  $X$ ;retained is membership in  $A\setminus Y$ ;adjacency is the original graph adjacency restricted to this subtype.Then all three hypotheses follow from the bundle definition and feasibility. This supplies the correct mathematical connection without imposing an additional physical assumption.The note expressly leaves the actual graph adapters and all- $r$  embedding outside the formalized scope. That is appropriate. The snippet does not by itself formally certify the coordinate fixture, the matching, the frozen witnesses for every translated endpoint, or the charge identities.9. Exactly which implication is disprovedThe example disproves regional nonpositivity inferred from the conjunction of:feasibility;occupied degree exactly three at every matching endpoint;acyclicity of both degree-three dependency digraphs;absence of both fixed-side threshold cores;absence of every nonempty oriented endpoint-promotion bundle;tile connectivity of the receiver; $\sigma=\eta=0$ .All those conditions hold while
$$\rho(R)=1.$$
Thus promotion normalization alone cannot eliminate every positive receiver. In particular, there is no first endpoint-promotion move available in this example, so a longer sequence of such moves cannot repair it either.The example does not disprove a theorem guaranteeing compensation from an appropriate exterior region. Its displayed donor provides exactly that compensation. Nor does bundle terminality establish objective optimality or maximal  $|T|$  under more general changes. As a concrete scope check, in the base board one can delete all four matching edges and add the four previously blank corners to  $T$ . The resulting sixteen selected vertices are independent, retain the original twelve selected vertices, and preserve objective  $16$ . This operation lies outside the endpoint-promotion bundle class.Finally, the corrected preceding bridge description now matches all three actual incidences, and its unchanged numerical formulas remain valid. The reported control counts, unspecified twelve-edge grid control, and historical horizontal-matching result are not needed for the accepted proofs and are not independently certified by this review.The corrected package earns ACCEPT as written mathematics: an exact fixed-side promotion criterion, a sound mixed-side exclusion certificate, a complete bundle-terminal positive receiver, its all-size connected extension, and an exact exterior repair. The universal compensation and grid questions remain open, and no full Lean formalization of this package is claimed.
